subject: Urban Planning
title: Environmental Racism and Land Use
description: A 60-second lesson on Environmental Racism and Land Use.

hook.text: In the US, hazardous waste sites are disproportionately located near minority communities. This is not a coincidence.

buildup.text: Industrial zoning in poor and minority neighborhoods makes them legal dumping grounds for polluting facilities.

discovery.text: Cancer Alley in Louisiana — 85 miles of petrochemical plants — runs through predominantly Black communities.

twist.text: When residents fight new plants, companies threaten to take jobs elsewhere. The choice: poison or poverty.

climax.text: The Environmental Justice movement demands that no community bear disproportionate environmental burden.

punchline.text: They zone pollution next to the powerless. The map is the weapon.

quiz.question: What is environmental racism in land use?
options: Banning all environmental regulations in minority neighborhoods
Disproportionately siting polluting facilities near minority communities
Charging higher environmental fees in predominantly white areas
